Second flush of pitchers just opened up a few days ago. Check out the red in the throat and how it goes down past the neck, unlike in "regular" rugelii's or mooreis with nice red throats. I think this characteristic came from the leah wilkerson parent plant. Are we getting closer to cracking the code on how to produce extreme red throats from "scratch?" Maybe so...

Oh, more updates on the origin of S. x Legacy. Spoke with Rob, and he grew out seeds from Brooks Garcia. Out of all the seeds, I believe they all died off except one plant, and it happened to be Legacy! How lucky is that?!

posts.body_html:
HI rmeyer,

Yes, Brooks Garcia is credited for breeding and creating this plant. Rob is the owner of the plant since he received the seeds and grew them out. He gave me one of the first divisions to ensure the survival of this plant, and although he didn't ask, out of respect, I told him I accepted this plant under the terms that he has the first rights to distributing/naming/publishing the plant. Also, he has the right to getting a piece back if all his original material bites the dust. I can't and won't release any divisions until he gives me permission to do so.

I have no credit whatsoever for this plant, I'm merely holding this plant on behalf of Rob as an insurance policy.

blackbean: I think everyone and their grandmother with the two parent plants have made this cross, including myself Still too early to tell, but out of probably more than 100 plants, there's maybe one so far that comes close, but too early to tell if it's anything spectacular like Legacy. Who knows, maybe there's even better ones in the batch, but from what I see so far, the majority of them aren't worth mentioning. Knowing this, having Legacy as the only survivor of a seed batch seems like some crazy luck to me!
